verdict.rationale: Ledgy lets admins create dedicated API service accounts for an integration such as an agent. These authenticate via OAuth 2.0 client_credentials with short-lived (24h) tokens, and the docs say the credentials are 'scoped per integration' and can be revoked immediately. However, nothing documents choosing permission scopes, read-only access, or per-operation or per-company restrictions, so least-privilege scoping depth is unproven. Missing for 10: documented selectable permission scopes or roles for service accounts, read-only or operation-level restriction, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can issue scoped/least-privilege API credentials for an agent

citations.quote: the credentials are scoped per integration, the tokens are short-lived, and revocation takes effect immediately
Create one in the Ledgy app under Company Settings → General → API service accounts
Exchange the credentials for an access token using the OAuth 2.0 `client_credentials` grant
Revoke deletes the service account and invalidates its outstanding access tokens right away.
